sections.name: Zoe and Grizzbolt (Tower boss)
sections.card:
Summary: She runs the Rayne Syndicate and is fought with her partner Grizzbolt in the Tower in the Windswept Hills. She is the first Faction Leader you are expected to fight and the easiest of them, at level 10 in normal mode and level 72 in hard mode.
Weak points: Grizzbolt is an Electric Pal that mostly uses Electric moves, so Ground-element Pals are the best answer. Early picks that work well are Gumoss, Rushoar and Fuddler, all easy to find. Dumud also works, but its Water side means Electric moves hit it for normal damage instead of being resisted. The Crossbow, which you can have by level 13, is usually the best weapon, and the Three Shot Bow suits Grizzbolt's large size.
Looks like: Zoe's hair is in two pigtails, black on the left and pink on the right. She has a black beanie with two ear-like shapes on it and a leather jacket in black, cut short, with the sleeves marked in pink.
Tips: Grizzbolt's Lightning Claw is hard to dodge, so if dodging is not your strength, lean on a shield to take the hits; circling behind the pillars avoids most of its attacks. Recalling your Pal just before Grizzbolt hits it, then sending it out again, spares it the damage and makes it attack faster. In hard mode a level 55 Syndicate Crusher joins the fight, and a Rocket Launcher makes short work of it. Grizzbolt then gains Grass moves too, Spine Vine and Seed Mine, which have a chance of leaving you ivy-covered, and a Grappling Gun helps you dodge while you are.

sections.name: Lily and Lyleen (Tower boss)
sections.card:
Summary: She leads the Free Pal Alliance and is fought with her partner Lyleen in the Tower on the Crescent Moon Shore. She is the second Faction Leader you are expected to fight, and in hard mode she is level 74.
Weak points: Lyleen is a Grass Pal that mostly uses Grass moves, so Fire Pals are the best answer, but it also has Water moves, such as Acid Rain and Bubble Blast, to counter them, so be careful. Vanwyrm resists its Grass attacks. Wixen's Partner Skill strengthens your attacks and gives them Fire damage for as long as it is out. The Fire Arrow Crossbow does extra damage to Lyleen and can burn it.
Looks like: Lily is barefoot, with short white hair marked by pale green streaks. Her green toga has gold lines on it, and on her forehead is a crown like a branch whose left side juts upward, set with rubies that stand for fruit.
Tips: Stay back when Lyleen uses Poison Fog, or you will be poisoned, and be ready for it to heal itself, which makes it tricky to finish off. In hard mode two level 55 Free Pal Alliance Devouts with Crossbows join the fight; kill them first, or their electric arrows will keep troubling you all through the battle. Lyleen then uses Water attacks more than Grass, so an Electric Pal that resists Water can help, and Flame Funnel is a top choice against it.

sections.name: Axel and Orserk (Tower boss)
sections.card:
Summary: He leads the Brothers of the Eternal Pyre and is fought with his partner Orserk in the Tower at the top of Mount Obsidian. He is the third Faction Leader you are expected to fight, at level 30 in normal mode and level 76 in hard mode. The arena has electrified grids that can be turned on at will to catch players off guard.
Weak points: Orserk is part Dragon and part Electric and attacks with both, so Ice and Ground Pals are the best answer. Reptyro Cryst resists everything Orserk throws and has high Defense, so it can soak up hits. Anubis is a strong attacker that gives your attacks Ground damage while it is out. Wumpo's Snow Bowling works very well against Orserk. In hard mode Orserk still has no Fire attacks, so Ice Pals stay effective.
Looks like: Axel is young and athletically built. His purple hair is tipped in yellow, shaped like lightning bolts, and his black beanie carries zigzags in yellow and purple.
Tips: Orserk's Kerauno attack hurts a lot, so avoid it where you can. In hard mode a level 55 Mossanda Lux and a level 55 Relaxaurus Lux join the fight; they are not tough, and area attacks clear them quickly. Orserk also gains Grass attacks such as Crosswind and Solar Blast to deal with Ground Pals. Frostallion and Gildane are good hard mode picks, since riding them adds Ice or Ground damage to your attacks.

sections.name: Marcus and Faleris (Tower boss)
sections.card:
Summary: He commands the Palpagos Islands Defense Force and fights alongside his partner Faleris in the Tower in the Desiccated Dunes. He is the fourth Faction Leader you are expected to fight, at level 40 in normal mode and level 78 in hard mode, and the first whose partner can fly.
Weak points: Faleris is a Fire Pal that mostly uses Fire moves, so Water Pals are the best answer, but it has a few Electric moves to counter them, so be careful. Azurobe gives your attacks Water damage while you ride it but is slow on land, so it tends to get hit; Suzaku Aqua strengthens its own Water attacks while mounted; Jormuntide is a good pick too, though its size makes it hard to dodge with. Curtain Splash and Hydro Slicer rank among the strongest moves to use on Faleris.
Looks like: Marcus is a tall man with a sturdy frame and a two-tone beard, brown streaked with black. His coat is a long, dark military one, with fur around the collar and a pair of stripes on each sleeve.
Tips: The Pump-action Shotgun, the Assault Rifle and the Semi-Auto Shotgun usually work best at this level. In hard mode he arrives with a team of level 55 PIDF Infantry and PIDF Elites, who are weak enough that area attacks clear them easily, and Selyne helps because its Partner Skill makes Holy Burst hit harder.

sections.name: Victor and Shadowbeak (Tower boss)
sections.card:
Summary: He runs the PAL Genetic Research Unit and is fought together with his partner Shadowbeak in the Tower in the Astral Mountains. He is level 50 in normal mode and level 80 in hard mode.
Weak points: Shadowbeak is a Dark Pal that mostly uses Dark moves, so Dragon Pals are the best answer, though it has some Ice moves to counter them. Jormuntide Ignis hits hard and takes only normal damage from those Ice moves, but it is big and hard to dodge with. Chillet gives your attacks Dragon damage while you ride it. Vanwyrm Cryst shrugs off every attack Shadowbeak has apart from Flame Funnel.
Looks like: Victor is a thin, pale man whose eyes are hidden behind a black blindfold. His wavy hair is black and white, and his long black coat is purple on the inside.
Tips: The Assault Rifle and Rocket Launcher usually work best at this level. In hard mode, when he and Shadowbeak drop to roughly 30 percent health, a clone of the pair appears, as strong as the originals and with the same attacks. You can tell the real ones because their health bar sits along the screen's upper edge, while the clone's hovers over its head; defeating the real pair removes the clone too, so go for them. Vampiric on your Pals together with area attacks such as Holy Burst and Air Blade heals you a lot, since the attacks should land on both.

sections.name: Bellanoir (Raid Boss)
sections.card:
Summary: A Dark Pal that does not live anywhere in the world: you summon it as a Raid Boss at a Summoning Altar with Bellanoir's Slab. Its health is 294,000, and it is the one Raid Boss with no Ultra form.
Weak points: Bellanoir attacks with Dark moves, so Dragon Pals are the best answer. Astegon takes very little damage from them, which makes it a solid tank; Orserk, Jormuntide and Jormuntide Ignis also resist its attacks and hit hard. Chillet gives your attacks Dragon damage while you ride it. For weapons, the usual choices are the Assault Rifle and Rocket Launcher.
Looks like: Tall and partly human in shape, its body looks like a black gown in motion. Red marks like eyes circle the waist, large blue-purple flames burn where the legs should be, and an antler-shaped growth juts from the left of the forehead.
Tips: Bellanoir is rated at about level 30 to 35, yet it is strong enough that you should reach about level 40 to 45 before trying it. Its Nightmare Ray hurts badly, so avoid it where you can. Choose the Raid Area rather than your base, since a Raid Boss can do widespread damage to a base, and you get ten minutes to win before it despawns and the raid fails.

sections.name: Summoning a Raid Boss (Summoning Altar and slabs)
sections.card:
Summary: Raid Bosses are the game's toughest fights: powerful Pals you summon yourself at a Summoning Altar, with ten minutes to win. They are Bellanoir, Bellanoir Libero, Blazamut Ryu, Xenolord, Hartalis and Moon Lord. All but Bellanoir also come in a stronger Ultra or Master version at level 80.
Tips: The Summoning Altar is unlocked at 33 in the Ancient Technology list, for 3 points. It costs 100 Stone and 20 Paldium Fragment and can only be built inside a Pal Base. Each boss needs its own slab: you put one together at most Handiwork stations from fragments you find in Treasure Chests or earn on Expeditions. Once the boss is summoned you pick between your own base and the Raid Area, and only one Raid Boss can be out at a time. If the ten minutes run out, the boss leaves and the raid is lost, and the damage it already did to your structures is not undone. A win drops Ancient Civilization Parts, Ancient Civilization Cores and Training Crystals, plus a Pal Egg that hatches into the boss, ordinary or Alpha; the Moon Lord drops no egg.

sections.name: Predator Pals
sections.card:
Summary: Extremely strong versions of ordinary Pals that always attack on sight and cannot be captured. A kill pays out 25 times the experience of the ordinary version. They are rare: now and then one spawns at random in place of a regular Pal instead of at a fixed spot, and only certain species can appear this way.
Looks like: Larger than the ordinary Pal, with eyes that shine red and a red aura around its body.
Tips: They use three Neutral-element skills. Predator Surge charges up, then explodes around the user; Predator Blast builds up power and releases a sustained beam; Predator Mark shoots three fast beams in a row. They are missing from the world map, but you can hear a low hum when one is close. Defeating one drops Predator Cores and Giant Pal Souls, but no Ancient Civilization Parts, and a first kill gives neither Ancient Technology Points nor Pal Bounty Tokens. Species that can appear include Direhowl at level 10 and Gildra at level 46.

sections.name: Bounty Targets
sections.card:
Summary: Named human enemies that act as world bosses at fixed spots on the map, each marked with an icon. They attack on sight, sometimes with a partner Pal, and come back after a set time once beaten.
Looks like: Larger than ordinary human characters, with glowing red eyes and a purple aura around them.
Tips: The higher a target's level, the more it asks of you: better equipment, stronger Pals, or just more planning. Every target drops Successful Bounty Tokens, and higher-level ones drop more; a Vigilante Bounty Officer swaps them for items. The first time you beat a target you also earn Ancient Technology Points. Ask a Bounty Intel Dealer for details on the targets in an area. Targets range from Scoot at level 10 to Ram at level 59, and some bring a partner Pal, such as Crash with a Direhowl.

sections.name: Skill Fruits
sections.card:
Summary: A consumable that teaches a Pal one Active Skill: you pick the fruit in your inventory and choose a Pal from your party.
Uses: Each fruit is tied to one skill, and the Pal's element need not match it, so Fire Pals can be taught Water moves. Any fruit can go to any Pal, whatever its element, and it can be used on caught humans too. Each skill fruit has a rarity from Uncommon to Epic and a power figure; Air Cannon is Uncommon with power 40, and Holy Burst is Epic with power 700.
Tips: Most grow on blue-tinted trees around the islands. Treasure Chests in Dungeons can hold them as well, and on rare occasions one spawns on the ground. Life Fruit, Power Fruit and Stout Fruit form a separate group of Legendary fruits, each adding 10 to a Pal's HP, Attack or Defense Potential.

sections.name: Pal Bounty Token
sections.card:
Summary: A key item you get the first time you defeat or catch an overworld Alpha Pal. Each one is tied to an element and gives your Pals a lasting boost to the Active Skills of its element.
Uses: The effect applies by itself and for good, with nothing to equip, and it only boosts Pal Active Skills, not your own weapons. Tokens come in small, medium and large grades worth +1%, +2% and +3%, and same-element tokens add together. Some high-level Alpha Pal areas stay closed until you hold certain tokens.
Tips: It is not the Successful Bounty Token, which comes from human Bounty Targets and is traded to a Vigilante Officer. You find these in the Key Items part of your inventory, and they cannot be spent, traded, sold or consumed. The same Alpha gives no further token after the first time.

sections.name: Lifmunk Effigy
sections.card:
Summary: A small green statue of a Pal, scattered across the islands, that you hand in at a Statue of Power to raise your capture power and make Pals easier to catch.
Uses: Put up a Statue of Power yourself, or come across one in the wild, interact with it, and spend effigies on the next capture power level. Each level costs more effigies than the one before. The bonus is worth the most near the end of the game, where plenty of high-level Pals can slip out of nearly every sphere. The Statue of Power unlocks at level 9 for 2 technology points.
Tips: They are easy to spot after dark from a long way off, thanks to their bright green glow. Search beyond the obvious spots: behind waterfalls, on top of rocky peaks and inside ruins are all worth checking, and a few sit hidden in crevices at ground level.

sections.name: Ancient Civilization Parts
sections.card:
Summary: A Rare crafting material that many Ancient Technology items and structures need, which merchants do not sell. It comes from Alpha and Lucky Pals and from certain Expeditions.
Uses: Many Ancient Technology items and structures need it. So do items made from Uncommon or better Schematics, and the Pal Labor Research Laboratory also takes it for research.
Tips: Anubis and Bastigor always drop 4 to 6 of it, and Bellanoir always drops 1 to 3. One part weighs 1 and sells for 100.

sections.name: Successful Bounty Token
sections.card:
Summary: A special currency you get from defeating Bounty Targets, with the tougher targets giving more tokens.
Uses: Hand them to a Vigilante Bounty Officer to buy items such as Ancient Pal Manuscripts, High Grade Technical Manuals and Pal Reversers.
Tips: No merchant sells them, so they only come from Bounty Targets. If you capture a target it still drops tokens, and butchering it afterwards drops them a second time, so you get twice as many. It is not the same as the Pal Bounty Token, which comes from Alpha Pals.
